verdict.rationale: React's markup is JSX, a JavaScript syntax extension (react-docs-2), and React documents TypeScript support via @types/react and @types/react-dom (react-docs-13). That implies typed markup, since JSX lives in the same file as the script. However, the evidence never states that JSX props and children are type-checked at compile time. React Compiler build errors and ESLint hook rules are adjacent features, not template type checking, so they earn no credit. Missing for 10: explicit docs that JSX/TSX markup (props, children, events) is type-checked at compile time, and independent or hands-on corroboration of template-level type errors.
